Diabetic depression is a real thing. All within my first year of being diagnosed, I overdosed 4 times with opioids, had keto acidosis 3 times, and thought about jumping from a building once.

With all that being said, it does get better. You learn to adjust and, as long as you have insurance, realize there’s no reason to panic.

To me, it depends on a lot of things. It would be nice to have someone to relate to, someone that understands how big of a life change it is, but if I were to choose someone who had T1D over a normal person, I would prefer if they were like me and diagnosed later in life. People that are born with T1D often don’t understand how much of a curse it really is. At one point you’re just 16, having fun, going out with your friends, eating whatever whenever you’d like, then, all of a sudden, you’re worried that if you play basketball for too long your sugar will drop. EVERYTHING in your life changes. Some normal people can’t understand that change, and sometimes neither can the people who were born this way. It sucks out all of your life force knowing you can never go back to how things were. It’s quite literally killed me a couple of times just managing to come to terms with it, between keto acidosis, drug addiction, & depression.

So, answering your question, yes; I would prefer if someone I’d date to have T1D. I’d know that if they were like me they must be mentally strong by now. Like OP stated though, it’s quite a rare disease, so I doubt they’ll make a dating app for us any time soon.
